item.title: Traders running a vehicle repair business on the public road, 28th September
item.description:
For the last few months, there has been running a vehicle repair business on Selby Road outside Shipley Court (SE20 8SE) and in the last 3 weeks it has expanded considerably. There are now vehicles parked on both sides of the road, including three flatbed trucks shown in the images. The repairs are carried out on the road outside of normal business hours and sometimes the vehicles being repaired have no number plates on while being parked on the road. It is causing significant disruption as parking space becomes very limited and only one direction of traffic can pass at a time, leading to cars queuing at either end of the bottleneck it creates, beeping nosily and then driving very fast to get through and prevent traffic building up. A couple of times fights have almost broken out. Car alarms are going off frequently and they are revving motorbikes into the evening. They seem to be now consciously expanding the space they take up and taking over more spaces every time someone moves their car and I’m worried it’s making the road very dangerous. The men running the business walk up and down the road constantly and so I haven’t been able to take a photo of them working because I do not want to be identified, but I can provide more evidence if it will not be shared further. At first I hoped more cars being parked on the road would be a traffic calming measure but it’s ended up making it much, much worse. There was a casualty on the road over Christmas last year and I’m worried this increases the risk. The road is used by schools for cycling proficiency lessons and so frequently has children around.

Nearest road to the pin placed on the map (automatically generated by OpenStreetMap): 1, Selby Road, Anerley, Greater London
Report on FixMyStreet

item.title: Fly-tipping on the public pavement outside 262 Woolwich Road, 28th September
item.description:
Hi there, There seem to be new tenants who have recently moved into the lower-level flat of the above address, and they appear to have dumped unwanted items from the flat onto the public pavement. When I explained to them that this constitutes fly-tipping and that they could potentially be fined, they told me that they had asked the council for a recycling bin and were told that they would only get one at the end of October. Could you please arrange for the fly-tipping to be removed and also address this with the residents of that flat? Whatever the situation with their bins, dumping unwanted items on the public pavement is a crime and needs addressing now, please.

Nearest address to the pin placed on the map (from OS Places API): Woolwich Road, Greenwich

item.title: Overgrown foliage forcing pedestrians and pushchairs towards the road, 28th September
item.description:
There is significant overgrown foliage at the bottom of Camdale Road which is encroaching across the public pavement and substantially reducing the usable width of the footpath. As the attached photographs demonstrate, pedestrians — including parents pushing prams — are being forced right towards the kerb and road in order to get around the vegetation. This is a pedestrian safety issue, not simply a cosmetic problem. The pavement needs to remain safely accessible for parents with pushchairs, young children, wheelchair users and people with limited mobility. Please arrange for the foliage to be properly cut back to the boundary/fence line so that the full usable width of the public pavement is restored. Please also ensure that the report is not marked as resolved until the obstruction has actually been cleared. This appears to be another example locally of vegetation being allowed to substantially encroach onto a public footway before action is taken. Please consider whether more regular inspection and preventative maintenance is required.

Nearest address to the pin placed on the map (from OS Places API): Camdale Road, Plumstead
Report on FixMyStreet
